messages:
Anya: Heads-up — during onboarding for redwood-7b-int8 we saw a positional drift that only shows up after shard rebalancing on long prompts (~48k+). Repro script attached below. Not a simple off-by-one; token alignments look fine until a sharp divergence after a KV handoff window.

Luke: which quant profile and runtime? int8f or int8a? and is this with the new shard-swap code?

Anya: int8f (quant-v2), runtime build: inference-2026.03.11-rc3, shard-swap enabled. Repro command:```bash
python reproduce_longctx.py --model redwood-7b-int8 --prompt tests/long_story.txt --max-tokens 72000 --seed 42 --use-kv-shard-swap
```
Small failing excerpt in the log: ```
[2026-03-11T14:02:17Z] PREFILL: tokens=49152 shard=3 start_idx=49120
[2026-03-11T14:02:17Z] HANDOFF: target_shard=4 warp_rotate=1
[2026-03-11T14:02:18Z] GENERATE: token=49153 expected="in" got="inn"
```

Sachin: hmm. That warp_rotate=1 line stands out. Could be RoPE frequency scaling mismatch when we compact or rotate a shard's cache. If the prefill uses absolute positions and the swapped-in cache assumes a different rotary base, you get phase slip. Do you see the same when running float16?

Anya: float16 baseline is stable: divergence ~0.004% up to 72k. int8 runs: token-diff metric is ~0.37% at 48k, then jumps to 2.8% after 64k in repeated runs. I captured diffs with our token-diff harness (attached).

Priya: two quick hypotheses: (1) quant kernel uses a different RoPE scaling factor (freq table rounding) when compressing keys, (2) the shard-swap path omits the per-shard position-offset normalization we added for dynamic windowing. Easy triage: run the same prefill but with forced zero-pad (no wrap) vs wraparound and compare token-diff. Also run quantized kernels with freq_table=ref (copy from f16) to see if it collapses.

DevBot: @Anya initiated longctx-bisect job #LCTX-778 with tags [int8, shard-swap, rope-check]. Estimated walltime 6h.

Luke: I can run the zero-pad vs wrap test on a dedicated T4. Will do the two variants and post numbers. If it reproduces only with wrap, that's a runtime handling bug. If both, then quant kernels.

Anya: thanks. Quick numbers from an early run:
- int8 wrap: token-diff @48k = 0.37%, @72k = 2.8%
- int8 zero-pad: token-diff @48k = 0.05%, @72k = 0.09%
- f16 wrap: token-diff @72k = 0.004%
So wrap/hand-off path with int8 looks like the culprit.

Sachin: solid repro. That difference between zero-pad and wrap is telling. Likely the quantized key representation loses phase precision at the wrap boundary. Suggest adding a short-term mitigation: align prefill to shard boundaries (force zero-pad up to next boundary) and switch to f16 fallback for sequences > 64k until we patch. Also add a unit-test that simulates warp_rotate=1 in CI for int8 kernels.

Priya: I'll prepare the unit test. Patch candidate: in kv_shard_swap() apply per-shard pos_offset normalization before compressing keys. This keeps the rotary base consistent. If that fixes tests, we can upstream to quant-kernels.

Luke: patching and testing now on LCTX-780 (dedicated long-run node). If I get green, will open PR against runtime and coordinate with kernel folks.

Anya: Action items:
- Luke: run full bisect + confirm unit test (LCTX-780).
- Priya: draft unit test and a small repro harness for kernel owners.
- Sachin: prepare mitigation plan for customer-facing fallback (shard-boundary padding + f16 beyond 64k).
- Anya: notify solutions and QA owning the long-context templates so we can monitor customer impact.

Anya: thanks all. If anyone finds a quick magic flag we can flip to disable wraparound on affected deployments, mention it here. Otherwise I'll coordinate the mitigation rollout tomorrow. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
